purpose: Prevent post-hoc subtraction of airglow/zodiacal/starlight or a hand-picked deep-night spectrum from rescuing the real-sky comparison after residuals are seen.

distinction.instrumentDarkCorrection: part of the externally documented Pandora calibration/product reduction and must follow the product definition
distinction.astrophysicalNightSkyBackground: real directional sky radiance from sources not generated by the frozen solar-twilight MYSTIC setup, including airglow, zodiacal light, integrated starlight and other night-sky emission/scattering

currentClaimChoice.primaryObservedQuantity: the calibrated absolute directional real-sky radiance delivered by the admitted Pandora product after its normal instrument corrections, with no validation-specific astrophysical deep-night subtraction
currentClaimChoice.reason: the current empirical question in MODEL_FORM_ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY is whether the frozen production-intended sky model reproduces independent absolute real-sky integrated radiance. Any mismatch caused by omitted night-sky emission remains model-form empirical error rather than being removed after seeing residuals.

diagnosticDeepNightEvidence.preferredReferenceRuleForDiagnostics: same site, same spectrometer, same pointing definition and calibration-valid period; deterministic nearest eligible deep-night observation by UTC with immutable ID tie-break

relationshipToPrior0074.reason: not subtracting a positive real-sky background cannot artificially reduce the observed-vs-model error of a solar-only model; it preserves the background as part of the model-form challenge. The inherited numeric gates are therefore not loosened by this choice.

lateTwilightInterpretation.ifBackgroundBecomesNonnegligibleNearTheD: preserve the resulting empirical residual/bias under the current generation
lateTwilightInterpretation.futureFix: a future model generation may add independently specified night-sky components, but the opened sessions cannot be reused as untouched validation for that replacement
